[[Image:gypsyweed.jpg|thumb|Heath speedwell in Oregon]]

'''''Veronica officinalis''''', the '''heath speedwell''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''common gypsyweed''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=VEOF2|taxon=Veronica officinalis|access-date=29 July 2015}}</ref> '''common speedwell''', or '''Paul's betony''', is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Plantago|plantain]] family [[Plantaginaceae]]. It is native to [[Europe]] and western [[Asia]]. It has been introduced to North America and is widely [[naturalisation (biology)|naturalised]] there.

==Description==
It is a [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] with hairy green stems {{convert|10-50|cm||0|abbr=on}} long that cover the ground in mats and send up short vertical shoots which bear soft violet flowers. The [[leaf|leaves]] are {{convert|1.5-5|cm||1|abbr=on}} and {{convert|1-3|cm||1|abbr=on}} broad, and softly hairy.
[[File:Heath Speedwell (Veronica officinalis) in Pennsylvania.jpg|alt=Heath speedwell in Pennsylvania|thumb|Heath speedwell in Pennsylvania]]
It flowers from May until August.

==Cultivation and uses==
This speedwell grows in open areas, such as fields, meadows and gardens, where it is sometimes grown as an edible, or [[medicinal herb]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Veronica+officinalis | title = Veronica officinalis | work = PFAF }}</ref>

The slightly bitter and astringent taste and tea-like smell of speedwell led to its use as a tea substitute in 19th-century France, where it was called ''thé d'Europe'', or "Europe tea". The French still use this term as a name for speedwell.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1kFBAAAAcAAJ&pg=PA132|title=Pharmacopoea Bavarica Iussu Regio Edita|date=1822|publisher=Joseph Lindauer|location=Munich|pages=132|language=la}}</ref>
